section: Kakatiya administration - Nayankara system, tank irrigation, trade, Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam
subsections: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items

accepted.s: Which one of the following guilds was primarily associated with domestic trade during the Kakatiya period?
accepted.x: Nakaram was the guild associated with domestic trade. Nanadesi Pekkandru specialised in foreign trade, while Ubhaya Nanadesi operated in both markets.
accepted.tq: Use the scope of each guild to distinguish closely related trade organisations.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Nanadesi Pekkandru guild was mainly connected with
accepted.x: Nanadesi Pekkandru was a foreign-trade guild. Nakaram was associated with domestic trade, whereas Ubhaya Nanadesi dealt in both domestic and foreign markets.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a similar-sounding guild name.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Nakaram — Domestic trade
2. Nanadesi Pekkandru — Foreign trade
3. Ubhaya Nanadesi Pekkandru — Domestic and foreign trade
4. Ayyavali Ainuraru — Guild of 500

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Nakaram handled domestic trade, Nanadesi foreign trade, Ubhaya Nanadesi both types of trade, and Ayyavali Ainuraru was the guild of 500.
accepted.tq: Check every pair against the guild’s specialised scope or numerical identity.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Virabanajam was licensed to operate in which of the following regions?
accepted.x: The Virabanajam guild was licensed for Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda, as recorded in the Tripurantakam inscription of 1282.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific licensed regions rather than confusing them with ports or foreign trading partners.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Tripurantakam inscription of 1282 is associated with the licensing of
o: Virabanajam in Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda
accepted.x: The Tripurantakam inscription of 1282 records the areas in which Virabanajam was licensed to operate: Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda.
accepted.tq: Link the inscription, date and guild through the distinctive licensing detail.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ayyavali Ainuraru is best described as
o: An official body collecting port duties
A guild restricted to domestic trade
accepted.x: Ayyavali Ainuraru was the great trans-regional merchant guild known as the guild of 500.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical identity in the guild’s name to identify the organisation.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a function or characteristic of the Kakatiya merchant guilds?
o: Exercising an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade
Maintaining their own seal or emblem
accepted.x: Guilds maintained seals or emblems, settled disputes and kept private military forces, but they did not possess an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade.
accepted.tq: Find the overbroad and exclusive statement that goes beyond the guild functions.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding merchant guilds:

1. A merchant was called a Behari.
2. Trade was referred to as Vyavaharam.
3. The head of a guild was called Setti or Sreshthi.
4. Guild members were drawn exclusively from Vaishyas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Guild members came from several communities, including Settis, Reddis, Nayakulu, Boyas, Dasaris and Vaishyas, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the exclusive-membership statement and retain the precise occupational terms.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the economic and administrative functions of merchant guilds?
o: Temple priests, military commanders and village headmen
Bankers, local administrators and negotiators for tax concessions
Coin minters, irrigation engineers and royal ambassadors
Judges, royal tax collectors and hereditary governors only
accepted.x: Merchant guilds acted as bankers and local administrators and negotiated with the king for tax concessions. The Motupalli charter illustrates this interaction.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that combines the guild’s economic, administrative and negotiating roles.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was included among the exports of the Kakatiya period?
o: Iron tools, salt and timber only
Perfumes, horses, porcelain and silk alone
Grain, copper and medicinal herbs alone
accepted.x: The listed exports were textiles, spices, diamonds and gold. Perfumes and spices were mentioned among the imports.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the export list from the shorter list of imports.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was mentioned as an import in Kakatiya overseas trade?
accepted.x: Perfumes were among the imports. Textiles, diamonds and gold were listed among the exports.
accepted.tq: Use the export-import reversal trap with commodities appearing in both trade contexts.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The Kakatiya trade network had commercial links with which of the following regions or countries?

1. China
2. Persia
3. Arabia
4. Ceylon
5. East Indies

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The recorded trading partners included China, Persia, Arabia, Ceylon and the East Indies.
accepted.tq: Verify the complete list instead of stopping after identifying the first few familiar partners.
accepted.sec: Trade - routes, merchant guilds and samayas, items  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ports collecting import and export duties were known as
accepted.x: Ports that collected import and export duties were called Kara Pattanam.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the technical term for duty-collecting ports from names of actual ports and guilds.

accepted.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam was issued by Ganapatideva in
accepted.x: Ganapatideva issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244 CE at Motupalli.
accepted.tq: Place the inscription date among the nearby dates associated with other inscriptions and periods.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam:

1. It guaranteed safety to foreign merchants.
2. It remitted arbitrary taxes.
3. It promised compensation for losses caused by shipwreck or theft.
4. It authorised harassment of merchants by local officials.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The charter protected foreign merchants, remitted arbitrary taxes and promised compensation for losses from shipwreck or theft. It stopped, rather than authorised, harassment by officials.
accepted.tq: Identify the reversed negative statement concerning official harassment.

accepted.s: Who was appointed at Motupalli under the Abhaya Sasanam of Ganapatideva?
accepted.x: Siddayya Devudu was the official posted at Motupalli under Ganapatideva’s charter.
accepted.tq: Match the official with the charter and port, avoiding confusion with later rulers and builders.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two Motupalli protection charters?

1. Ganapatideva’s Abhaya Sasanam was issued in 1244 CE.
2. A later bilingual Telugu-Tamil charter was issued by Anavota Reddi.
3. The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam of 1416 was associated with Deva Raya I.
4. The 1416 Dharma Sasanam belonged to the reign of Ganapatideva.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The 1416 Motupalli Dharma Sasanam belonged to Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya I, not Ganapatideva.
accepted.tq: Separate similar charters by issuer, date and dynasty.

accepted.s: In the expression ‘Abhaya Sasanam’, the word ‘Abhaya’ conveys the idea of
accepted.x: ‘Abhaya’ means assurance of safety. The charter used this principle to protect foreign and seafaring traders.
accepted.tq: Use the literal meaning of the key term to identify the charter’s purpose.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Arikesari Samudram — Prola II
2. Ramappa tank — Recherla Rudra
3. Pakhala tank — Mummadi Nayaka
4. Laknavaram — Ganapatideva
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Arikesari Samudram was built by Prola II, Ramappa tank by Recherla Rudra, Pakhala tank by Mummadi Nayaka, and Laknavaram by Ganapatideva.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure builder-tank pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped ruler or tank.

accepted.s: Who constructed the Ghanapuram tank?
accepted.x: Ghanapuram tank was constructed by Ganapatideva.
accepted.tq: Test a direct builder-tank association from the irrigation record.

accepted.s: Bayyaram tank is associated with which builder?
o: Surambika, wife of Peda Komati Vema
Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka
accepted.x: Bayyaram tank was built by Mailamba, the sister of Ganapati.
accepted.tq: Use the kinship detail to distinguish the builder from other tank patrons.

accepted.s: Kunda Samudram, also called Chouda Samudram, was associated with
accepted.x: Kunda Samudram or Chouda Samudram was associated with Kundamamba and Malyala Chauda respectively.
accepted.tq: Combine alternative names with their associated patrons to avoid splitting one tank into two unrelated entries.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Pakhala tank was built by Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka, not by Mailamba. Mailamba was associated with Bayyaram tank.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped builder by comparing patrons of neighbouring tanks.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following statements about tank irrigation is correct?

1. Large tanks were called Samudrams.
2. Golusukattu cheruvulu were linked chain tanks.
3. Surplus water could pass downhill from one tank to the next.
4. Dashabandhamu referred to tax-free land assigned for tank maintenance.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Samudrams were large tanks, Golusukattu cheruvulu formed linked chains, surplus flowed to lower tanks, and Dashabandhamu was tax-free land for upkeep.
accepted.tq: Confirm the complete irrigation-system description, including the maintenance arrangement.

accepted.s: Tank-building was counted among the Sapta Santanalu, which refers to
accepted.x: Sapta Santanalu means seven meritorious works. The list included a son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a cultural-religious classification from administrative and fiscal categories.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT included among the Sapta Santanalu?
accepted.x: The Sapta Santanalu included son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure. A merchant guild was not one of the seven meritorious works.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the item belonging to trade rather than the list of meritorious works.

accepted.s: The Porumamilla tank inscription is associated with which combination?
o: 1369, Bhaskara, son of Bukka I, Vijayanagara period
1416, Deva Raya I, Motupalli, Reddi period
accepted.x: The Porumamilla tank inscription dates to 1369 and was issued by Bhaskara, son of Vijayanagara ruler Bukka I. It belongs to the Vijayanagara period and lists twelve requisites of a good tank.
accepted.tq: Combine date, person, dynasty and inscription subject to separate similar records.

accepted.s: The Porumamilla inscription is particularly important in the study of irrigation because it
o: records the twelve requisites of a good tank
defines the five classes of merchant guilds
records the tax rates on imported perfumes
lists the foreign merchants protected at Motupalli
accepted.x: The Porumamilla inscription of 1369 lists twelve requisites of a good tank. It is from the Vijayanagara period, though it is often studied alongside Kakatiya irrigation works.
accepted.tq: Identify the inscription from its distinctive technical subject rather than its dynasty alone.
